title: Provenance and the commons

open.what: Pylon on the painted harbour sets a cone on a paper boat that has just washed in: a claim nobody has checked. No words.

close.what: Back on the harbour: the boat now carries its manifest; Pylon reads it, leaves the call to the viewer, and the film ends.

segments.heading: Provenance and the commons
lines: Provenance and the commons.
A commons is anything people share and draw from, like open data or open source code. What keeps it usable?

segments.heading: One small library
lines: Start with a small compression library called xz.
In 2022 its maintainer wrote that it was an unpaid hobby project.
A helpful newcomer had been sending patches since 2021. Within months, the maintainer called the newcomer practically a co-maintainer.
In February 2024, the newcomer signed and shipped a new release.
Part of a backdoor sat only in the release download, and not in the public source.
An engineer caught it because remote logins ran about half a second slow.

predict.question: How could anyone downstream have checked that the download matched the source?

segments.heading: The wrong lesson
lines: In 1968, Garrett Hardin wrote that freedom in a commons brings ruin to all.
Many readers took the lesson that a commons needs a private owner or an outside ruler.
Hardin himself asked for coercion agreed on by the people affected.

segments.heading: What lasting commons do
lines: Elinor Ostrom compared shared fisheries, forests and irrigation systems that lasted with ones that failed.
In the ones that lasted she found eight design principles.
Most of the people the rules affect take part in making and changing them.
The people who watch for cheating are the users, or people the users can hold to account.
A review of over a hundred studies found that about two thirds supported her principles.
Across 178 forest user groups, more monitoring went with denser forest.

segments.heading: Where provenance gets lost
lines: One audit traced the licences of 1,858 datasets used to train AI.
On GitHub, 72 percent were listed with no licence at all.
In 29 percent, the licence listed was looser than the author's own terms.
Tracing each one back to where it was made cut the missing share to 30 percent.
Meanwhile, in one year about 5 percent of a widely used training corpus became fully closed to AI crawlers.

predict.question: When a dataset is copied to a popular site, how often does its licence survive the trip?

segments.heading: A record made at the source
lines: In software, a provenance record says where, when and how a release was built.
With it, anyone can check a download against its source.

segments.heading: What this does not prove
lines: Ostrom's cases are fisheries and forests. Applying them to code and data is our inference.
The licence audit counts missing records. It does not measure harm.
And a provenance record alone would not have stopped xz. Most of the backdoor was in the public source, signed by a maintainer people trusted.

segments.heading: Two things to keep
lines: Two things to keep. Record where a thing came from at the moment it is made.
And let the people who depend on it make the rules and check them.
The voice you heard is a synthesized version of mine. Every number on screen links to its source under the video.

items.text: Record where a thing came from when it is made.
Let the people who depend on it make the rules.
